A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5% of USCs have germline loss of function mutations in BRCA, TP53, or CHEK2.
5% of USC subjects have germline loss of function mutations in 3 genes: BRCA, TP53, or CHEK2.
5% of patients with serous carcinoma of the uterus have germline loss of function mutations in BRCA, TP53, or CHEK2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a significant proportion (5%) of women with uterine serosucarcomas carry germline mutations of tumor suppressor genes and that these mutations are not limited to BRCA1 and TP53, but also CHEK2.
the frequency of germline mutations among women with USC is higher than expected.
the risk of germline mutations is higher than expected for women with uterine serosus carcinoma and breast cancer.
